questions.question: Which AWS service provides a fully managed environment to build, train, and deploy machine learning models at scale?
options: Amazon Rekognition
Amazon Comprehend
AWS Glue
Amazon SageMaker
questions.explanation: Amazon SageMaker is the end-to-end managed ML platform on AWS that covers data labeling, training, tuning, deployment, and monitoring. Rekognition, Comprehend and Glue are higher-level or data-prep services.

questions.question: Which Amazon service is purpose-built for generative AI applications using foundation models from multiple providers via a single API?
options: Amazon Forecast
Amazon Polly
Amazon Lex
Amazon Bedrock
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock is a fully managed service that exposes foundation models (Anthropic Claude, Meta Llama, Mistral, Amazon Titan, etc.) through a single serverless API for building generative AI apps.

questions.question: A company wants to extract entities, key phrases and sentiment from customer support tickets. Which AWS service is the best fit?
options: Amazon Kendra
Amazon Transcribe
Amazon Translate
Amazon Comprehend
questions.explanation: Amazon Comprehend is the NLP service that detects entities, key phrases, language, sentiment, and PII in text. Translate handles language translation, Transcribe converts speech to text, and Kendra is enterprise search.

questions.question: A team is integrating a large language model into a customer-support assistant. They notice that small changes in how they word the request — adding examples, specifying tone, asking the model to think step by step — dramatically change the output quality without changing model weights. What is the primary purpose of the discipline that systematises these changes?
options: Cleaning training data and feature-engineering a tabular dataset before passing it to a supervised learning pipeline for batch training
Crafting input text
Re-training the underlying model on customer transcripts to adapt its weights to the company's domain — distinct from rewording inputs
Quantising the model from 16-bit to 8-bit weights to reduce inference cost, with no behavioural effect on outputs
questions.explanation: Prompt engineering is the practice of designing the text input so that a foundation model produces accurate, on-task responses without modifying the model's weights. Quantization, retraining and encryption are unrelated optimization or security activities.

questions.question: A product team has a public LLM that has no knowledge of internal product manuals updated last week. They want answers grounded in those manuals without retraining the model. Their solution: index the manuals, retrieve top passages by similarity at request time, and inject them into the prompt as context. Which technique is this?
options: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback — adjusts model weights using human preference data, but does not inject runtime context from external documents
Knowledge distillation — trains a smaller student model on a teacher's outputs, addressing model size and not real-time grounding
Retrieval-Augmented Generation
Few-shot prompting — embeds a handful of example input/output pairs in the prompt; useful for behaviour shaping but not a retrieval mechanism
questions.explanation: RAG retrieves relevant documents from a knowledge base (often a vector store) at inference time and injects them into the prompt, so the model can answer with private or fresh data without changing its weights. RLHF, fine-tuning and quantization all modify the model itself.

questions.question: A team wants to store embeddings to power a semantic search feature on top of Amazon Bedrock. Which AWS service provides a managed vector database capability?
options: Amazon DynamoDB with TTL-driven streams
AWS Step Functions Express workflows
Amazon OpenSearch Service (k-NN engine)
Amazon Athena federated SQL queries
questions.explanation: Amazon OpenSearch Service supports k-NN and a vector engine for storing and querying embeddings. Aurora PostgreSQL with pgvector and Amazon MemoryDB also support vectors, but among the listed options OpenSearch is the correct managed vector store.

questions.question: Which AWS Generative AI service is an enterprise assistant that can be grounded on a company's own data and integrated into business workflows?
options: Amazon Polly
Amazon Personalize
AWS DeepRacer
Amazon Q
questions.explanation: Amazon Q is a generative AI-powered assistant designed for work, able to connect to enterprise data sources (S3, Confluence, Salesforce, etc.) and answer questions, summarize and take actions while respecting access controls.

questions.question: A team is choosing the right ML paradigm for a fraud-detection problem. They have a large historical dataset where each past transaction is labelled fraud or legitimate by investigators. They want a model that learns to predict the label on new transactions. Which paradigm fits?
options: Unsupervised learning — operates on unlabelled data to discover structure (clusters, anomalies, embeddings); does not predict known target labels
Supervised learning — learns a mapping from input features to a known target label using a labelled training set, then predicts the label on unseen examples
Reinforcement learning — learns by interacting with an environment that returns rewards; not driven by a fixed labelled dataset of past examples
Self-supervised learning — generates pretext tasks from raw data and is a pretraining strategy, not the final stage for a fraud classifier with labelled data
questions.explanation: Supervised learning trains a model on input-output pairs (labeled data) to predict labels for new inputs. Unsupervised finds structure in unlabeled data; reinforcement learns by reward signals.

questions.question: A model performs extremely well on the training set but poorly on unseen data. What is this called?
options: Overfitting
Data drift
Underfitting
Bias
questions.explanation: Overfitting means the model has memorized the training data including its noise, so it generalizes poorly. Common mitigations: more data, regularization, simpler models, dropout, or early stopping.

questions.question: A regulated lender deploys a credit-scoring model and must demonstrate to auditors which features drove each decision and whether the model exhibits bias across demographic groups. AWS markets a service that surfaces feature attributions and bias metrics across the model lifecycle. Which service is it?
options: Amazon Macie — discovers and protects sensitive data in S3 via ML-based classification, not a model-explainability tool
Amazon Comprehend — a managed NLP service for entity / sentiment / language detection; not a bias-and-explainability product
Amazon SageMaker Clarify
Amazon Rekognition — image / video analysis service; not a generic ML-explainability product
questions.explanation: SageMaker Clarify provides bias detection on data and models and uses SHAP values for explainability of predictions. Ground Truth handles labeling, Pipelines orchestrates ML workflows, Feature Store stores features.

questions.question: A media app needs to convert article text into natural-sounding speech in multiple languages and voices. The team wants a managed AWS service that handles neural text-to-speech without operating their own infrastructure. Which service does this?
options: Amazon Transcribe — automatic speech recognition (audio to text), the opposite direction of what the team needs
Amazon Polly
Amazon Translate — neural machine translation between text languages; does not synthesise speech
Amazon Lex — conversational interface (chatbot) builder; uses ASR + NLU but is not primarily a text-to-speech engine
questions.explanation: Amazon Polly is the text-to-speech (TTS) service. Transcribe is the reverse (speech-to-text), Translate is for language translation, and Lex is for conversational chatbots.

questions.question: A retailer wants per-user product recommendations as a managed service. They don't want to design embeddings or train models themselves — they will hand AWS their interaction events (views, purchases) and the catalogue, and consume a real-time API. Which AWS service does this?
options: Amazon Forecast — time-series forecasting service; not designed for per-user recommendations from interaction events
Amazon Personalize
Amazon Kendra — enterprise search with semantic ranking; useful for document retrieval but not product recommendation
Amazon Lookout for Metrics — anomaly detection on business metrics; unrelated to user-personalisation use cases
questions.explanation: Amazon Personalize is a managed recommendation engine inspired by Amazon.com's own algorithms. Forecast is for time-series forecasting, Fraud Detector for fraud, and Lookout for Metrics for anomaly detection.

questions.question: A team is asked to define the term that describes large models pretrained on broad unlabelled data and then adapted via prompting, RAG, or fine-tuning to many downstream tasks — text, code, image, and beyond. Which option BEST describes a foundation model?
options: A large model trained on broad, mostly unlabelled data and adaptable to a wide range of downstream tasks via prompting, RAG, or fine-tuning
A narrow, single-task model trained on a small labelled dataset for a specific business objective — the opposite of foundation
A rules engine handcrafted by domain experts and frozen at deployment, with no statistical training component
A privacy-preserving algorithm that learns from federated edge devices without ever ingesting central training data
questions.explanation: Foundation models are large pretrained models (often LLMs or multimodal) trained on broad, diverse data that can be adapted via prompting, RAG or fine-tuning to many downstream tasks.

questions.question: A bank already has a public LLM responding well over their indexed compliance manuals via retrieval-augmented generation. Now they want the model itself to adopt their specific tone, terminology, and structured response format CONSISTENTLY across all answers — beyond what context injection achieves. When should fine-tuning be preferred over RAG?
options: When the team wants the model to change its tone, terminology, structured output style, or task-specific behaviour CONSISTENTLY, beyond what
When the underlying knowledge changes daily, since fine-tuning incorporates real-time updates faster than indexing new documents
Whenever the prompt exceeds 4,000 tokens, because RAG cannot operate above that limit on any foundation model
When fine-tuning is cheaper than RAG at every scale — fine-tuning has lower upfront cost than building a retrieval index
questions.explanation: Fine-tuning is best when you need to teach the model a stable behavior, tone, format, or domain vocabulary not learned during pretraining. For frequently changing knowledge, RAG is preferable because you only update the data store rather than the model.

questions.question: Which AWS Bedrock feature lets you create a managed knowledge base and have a model answer questions grounded on your private documents?
options: Bedrock Knowledge Bases
Bedrock Model Evaluation
Bedrock Provisioned Throughput
Bedrock Guardrails
questions.explanation: Knowledge Bases for Amazon Bedrock implements a managed RAG pipeline: ingest documents, chunk + embed them, store vectors and let models answer grounded questions. Guardrails enforces safety policies; Model Evaluation compares models; Provisioned Throughput reserves capacity.

questions.question: Which Bedrock feature helps block harmful content, profanity, prompt injection, and topics you do not want a model to discuss?
options: Bedrock Guardrails
Bedrock Knowledge Bases
Bedrock Studio
Bedrock Agents
questions.explanation: Guardrails for Amazon Bedrock allow you to define content filters, denied topics, word filters, sensitive-information filters, and contextual grounding checks for foundation models.

questions.question: A team trained a binary classifier on a highly imbalanced fraud dataset (1% positive). Accuracy looks great at 99% but the model is useless because it predicts 'not fraud' constantly. Which metric is MOST appropriate to evaluate this binary classifier on imbalanced data?
options: Accuracy — proportion of all correct predictions; misleading on imbalanced datasets where the majority class dominates
Area under the Precision-Recall curve (or F1 score) — focuses on the positive class's precision and recall, robust to extreme class imbalance
Mean Squared Error — regression metric that does not apply to a classification problem with discrete labels
Cross-entropy loss alone — useful as a training signal, but a single training-loss value does not characterise classifier quality on imbalanced data
questions.explanation: On imbalanced datasets, accuracy can be misleading (a model predicting only the majority class still scores high). F1-score balances precision and recall, making it more meaningful. MSE and R^2 are regression metrics.

questions.question: Under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model for AI services such as Amazon Bedrock, which task remains the customer's responsibility?
options: Maintaining the underlying foundation model's weights and inference infrastructure
Patching the GPU host operating systems and hypervisors running the foundation models
Choosing prompts, fine-tuning data, and evaluating model outputs for their use case
Securing physical access to AWS data centers and the underlying compute hardware
questions.explanation: AWS manages the infrastructure, hardware, and the hosted foundation models themselves. The customer is responsible for how they use the service: input data, prompt design, fine-tuning data, evaluation of outputs and downstream application controls.

questions.question: AWS publishes guidance for building generative-AI applications responsibly. A team building a customer-facing assistant studies the framework and identifies a recurring principle that includes fairness, explainability, privacy, security, and human oversight as core attributes of trustworthy AI systems. Which option captures a key principle of Responsible AI on AWS?
options: Maximising model size — always train the largest possible model and discard smaller alternatives, since size guarantees responsible behaviour
Building AI that is fair, explainable, secure, privacy-preserving, robust, and subject to human oversight, with transparency about training data and behaviour
Eliminating human reviewers entirely — automated decisions are inherently fairer than any process that includes human-in-the-loop validation
Hiding model behaviour from end users by default, on the basis that transparency invites adversarial probing rather than building trust
questions.explanation: AWS describes Responsible AI around dimensions like fairness, explainability, privacy, security, robustness, governance and transparency. SageMaker Clarify, Bedrock Guardrails and Model Cards help operationalize these principles in practice.

questions.question: A solutions architect needs to call a foundation model from a Lambda function with the lowest operational overhead. Which approach is best?
options: Deploy the model on an Amazon EKS cluster with GPU node groups
Train a custom model in SageMaker and host it on a real-time endpoint
Self-host the model on EC2 GPU instances behind an Application Load Balancer
Invoke a foundation model via the Amazon Bedrock runtime API from Lambda
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock exposes foundation models through a serverless API (InvokeModel / Converse). Calling Bedrock from Lambda gives you on-demand foundation model access with no servers, scaling, or model management on the customer side.
